propositions: Two test-only real-time windows (15s loopback server and 1s per-attempt deadline) consume multi-second wall time per test despite production semantics being about throughput/retry schedule/cleanup rather than elapsed time.
The snapshot-fetch test must retain a real loopback socket transferring above the configured floor for more than one complete injected low-speed window while reducing the window from 10s to 1s.

The ACLI subprocess-timeout test must launch exactly _MAX_ATTEMPTS real child processes, record the exact logical retry schedule [2, 4] without sleeping through actual backoff delays, and verify all spawned PIDs are absent after terminal failure.
Production timeout, stall, grace, drain, attempt, and backoff defaults must remain byte-unchanged with no production code modifications.
Both test files must pass in low single-digit seconds without absolute upper-bound assertions or runner/skip/xfail changes.
